_meta.label: Credia Finance
_meta.summary: Cosmos-native over-collateralized lending protocol on Terra phoenix-1 (NOT a swap dex). CosmWasm contracts (portfolio/oracle/config/liquidator) + NestJS indexer + GraphQL API. Accepts TLA ampLP tokens as collateral with a 2% fixed take rate — a candidate source of the contract-initiated gauge tributes. Per-asset cw20 receipt tokens carry the vca prefix (e.g. vcawbtc = the gauge's wBTC.creda.a entry).
_meta.provenance_note: Doc facts verified against the creda-docs repo @ main, 2026-07-16. Chain facts verified by browser LCD probes 2026-07-16. Observed platform values come from a decoded metrics query captured from the live app the same day — dated snapshots, not live bindings.

facts.claim: Credia is an over-collateralized lending protocol (supply/borrow/liquidate), not a swap dex. Suppliers earn interest; borrowers post collateral within per-asset LTV limits.
facts.notes: Matters for TLA Stats architecture: the dex-data 'credia' adapter models lending MARKETS, not swap pools.

facts.claim: The Portfolio contract (core lending logic: supply, borrow, repay, withdraw, liquidation, health monitoring) is terra1y6hfmr3lxxj6srduhlfz96x7sga2984pr757a0nrfuqxa9rqxapqcjv4zz.
facts.notes: Cross-confirmed on chain 2026-07-16: this address answers the metrics smart query (credia.query.metrics).

facts.claim: The Oracle contract (price feeds with EMA smoothing and validation) is terra1wj56ld9e9tuuw6qqr8m5ac8h953te65jcxz7c0dgekrud8lxwjgqryuwg3.
The Global Config contract (central registry for contract addresses, ownership, and protocol parameters) is terra1skhnhcj653zfkqzd4txcashg0qu4v0vnpckeztgmsm46cqn33lhsxyej6c.
The Liquidator contract (flashloan-based liquidation execution) is terra14452q6ypfn7xaque0hu8y9420xwu3y9gq7zw8f9rc82tx7rk2hlq8a7ca3.

A single smart query {"metrics":{}} on the Portfolio contract returns the entire platform state: total supplied/borrowed/collateral/reserves in USD, plus per-market oracle price, supplied/borrowed/collateral (raw + USD), utilization, supply/borrow APY, indices, LTV, liquidation threshold and penalty, caps, isolation config, take_rate, reserve_factor, and the proxy/vproxy receipt-token addresses.
facts.notes: Discovered from the live app's network traffic; the frontend makes this exact query (via phoenix-rpc.erisprotocol.com abci_query). This is the single data source the TLA Stats credia adapter captures from.

facts.claim: As of 2026-07-16 Credia listed 11 markets: LUNA, ampLUNA, arbLUNA, wBTC (Eureka-route ibc/8838…), USDC (ibc/2C96…), PAXG (ibc/0EF5…), wstETH (ibc/A356…), solidLUNA-family (ibc/8D52…), and three TLA ampLP tokens (gauge pools 32/project, 46/bluechip, 52/single). Platform totals: ~$650.9K supplied, ~$178.6K borrowed, ~$523.4K collateral.
facts.notes: Dated observation, NOT a live binding — the roster and totals change. Once the credia adapter is live, current values come from dex-data/credia snapshots instead of this fact.

facts.claim: Credia's take rate is a dynamic annual fee on SUPPLIED balances, configured per asset via governance as either a fixed percentage (e.g. 2% yearly) or a utilization-based curve. It is separate from the reserve factor, which takes a portion of borrower interest.

The three TLA ampLP collateral markets (Eris Alliance Hub factory tokens for gauge pools 32/project, 46/bluechip, 52/single) each carried take_rate {fixed: 0.02} — a 2% annual fee on supplied ampLP — with LTV 0.45 and roughly $150K total ampLP posted, as observed 2026-07-16. No other Credia market carried a take_rate.
facts.notes: Dated on-chain observation. Parameters are governance-set and can change.

facts.claim: OUR HYPOTHESIS (unconfirmed): the 2% take rate Credia collects on TLA ampLP collateral is a source of the contract-initiated add_bribe tributes to the TLA gauge — the tribute class the pre-2.3.0 event capture was blind to. To be confirmed against captured add_bribe sender addresses once bribe_capture data accumulates (first capture: 2026-07-19 epoch flip).
facts.notes: Explicitly labeled a hypothesis, not a sourced fact. If confirmed, Credia becomes a named, quantified briber for the bribe-source attribution work; if refuted, this fact gets corrected — never silently deleted.

facts.claim: Each Credia market deploys a per-asset cw20 token-proxy contract that represents supplied balances (the receipt token). Receipt symbols use the vca prefix; e.g. vcawbtc (terra1jjvy4s4tyw3ym6s3wk896up6jthvha9vtwaetah3z33sd788lttswhrcpc, decimals 8) is the receipt for supplied wBTC, listed on the TLA gauge as wBTC.creda.a. Each market's metrics entry exposes proxy_addr and vproxy_addr.
facts.notes: vcawbtc identity chain-verified 2026-07-16 via token_info (name/symbol vcawbtc, decimals 8). The token has no cw20 minter extension — minting is proxy-internal. This resolves the wBTC.creda.a gauge entry (2.69M VP) that was missing from identity.

facts.claim: Rates are utilization-driven with piecewise curves (gentle at low utilization, steep near the top). Supply APY ≈ Borrow APY × Utilization × (1 − Reserve Factor). Interest accrues continuously via growing supply/borrow indices over constant virtual amounts (real = vtotal × index).
facts.notes: Virtual-amount system detailed in developers/contracts/overview (AssetState: supply_vtotal, borrow_vtotal, supply_index, borrow_index). The GraphQL portfolio API returns vamounts — convert with the market indices.

facts.claim: The oracle aggregates multiple price sources with median/weighted methods, EMA smoothing, deviation limits, freshness checks, and circuit breakers. Assets are categorized (Major: minimal smoothing; Stable: tight validation; LongTail: enhanced smoothing; LP: derived from underlying assets and pool math).
facts.source_section: How We Source And Validate Prices
facts.notes: Credia oracle prices appear per-market in the metrics query. TLA Stats does NOT adopt them as its own pricing (PRICING-DOCTRINE.md governs); they are recorded in raw as Credia's view.

facts.claim: Health Factor = (collateral value × liquidation threshold) / total debt; positions become liquidatable when HF < 1.0. Liquidators repay debt up to a close factor and receive collateral at a discount (liquidation bonus).
facts.notes: Observed per-market params 2026-07-16 (e.g. ampLUNA: ltv 0.7, liquidation_threshold 0.72, liquidation_penalty 0.1; ampLP markets: ltv 0.45).

facts.claim: Isolation Mode contains riskier collateral: while an isolated asset is enabled as collateral no other collateral can be mixed, only whitelisted assets may be borrowed, each with individual caps plus a total USD cap; exiting requires fully withdrawing the isolated asset.
facts.notes: Per-market isolation config appears in metrics.assets[].state.isolation.

facts.claim: Efficiency Mode (EMode) applies group LTV/liquidation parameters to tightly correlated assets (e.g. LUNA + its LSTs, or stablecoins), raising borrowing power within the group (docs example: LUNA group 93% LTV vs 70% standalone). Collateral must stay within a single group.

Credia serves an indexer-backed GraphQL API at https://api.creda.finance/api/graphql with production queries for portfolios (per-address supply/borrow positions, LTHF), transaction history (typed events incl. full liquidation records), and marketHistories (time series of borrow_rate, supply_rate, utilization_rate, total_supplied, total_borrowed per denom).
facts.notes: marketHistories is an off-chain historical-rates source if we ever want Credia rate history without having captured it ourselves — an indexer database, so trust accordingly (chain state remains authoritative). The API also serves referral/points data; not relevant to TLA Stats.

facts.claim: The Credia backend is a NestJS indexer consuming contract events into Postgres (Prisma), served by Apollo GraphQL + REST, with BullMQ/Redis jobs for prices, snapshots, and notifications.
The Credia frontend reads chain state through phoenix-rpc.erisprotocol.com (abci_query SmartContractState) rather than an LCD; market data comes from the single metrics query, not GraphQL.
facts.notes: Observed from the live app 2026-07-16. The TLA Stats adapter uses our standard LCD endpoints for the same query instead of depending on Eris RPC.
